turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I compared the pool compositions against high-zT regions in the training set, giving most weight to close composition analogues rather than extrapolating from isolated outliers.

Most promising regions in the training data were:

- **Te–Pb near Te≈0.50, Pb≈0.45**: training examples reach ~0.73–0.78, matching **c037** very closely.
- **Sn-rich single-component region**: Sn≈0.556 has target ~0.71, matching **c010**.
- **Mg–Sn–Si/Sb family**: several nearby training samples around Mg≈0.66–0.68, Sn≈0.18–0.20, Si≈0.12 have targets ~0.50–0.65, favoring **c049** and also **c046**.
- **Sb–Co with small In/trace additions**: nearby high training samples reach ~0.53–0.70, favoring **c096**.

Ranked selection:

Final: c037, c010, c049, c096, c046
